title: President pledges tax cuts in 2027 Budget | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:34
-     - 342

President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has pledged further tax cuts in next month’s Budget, saying the reductions would be made without jeopardising the Government’s revenue target.

Addressing the National Convention of the National Intellectuals Organisation (NIO) at the P.D. Sirisena Grounds in Maligawatta, Colombo, on Saturday, the President said the Government had met its revenue targets, unlike in the past, when projected State income was not fully realised.

“In 2025, we exceeded the revenue target: our revenue reached 110% of the estimated level. Some people ask: ‘Isn’t it easy to raise revenue by imposing taxes?’ We would like to tell you that, after taking power, we did not impose a single new tax. We also reduced existing taxes to a considerable extent. In the forthcoming Budget, too, we will reduce some taxes. But we will do so without jeopardising our revenue target,” he said.

He said public debt, which stood at about 114% of GDP in 2022, would be brought down to between 90% and 95%.

President Dissanayake said Sri Lanka was yet to achieve the economic and social transformation people voted for two years ago, as his Government had spent its first two years laying the economic foundations needed for such a change. He urged professionals to support his reforms.

“Our challenge during the first two years has been to establish the economic conditions necessary for an economic transformation. If we compare the past two years, we have made considerable progress in preparing the economic foundations,” he said.

The President said Sri Lanka had recorded its lowest budget deficit in recent times last year, along with a current account surplus of $ 1.8 billion, the largest in the country’s history.

“Previously, there had been only about three occasions when the current account showed a surplus. On all three occasions, it was close to or below $ 300 million. That is economic progress; it is not an economic transformation,” he said.

Acknowledging the rise in the cost of living, President Dissanayake blamed it mainly on higher energy costs.

“The rise in inflation has made it more difficult for our people to purchase goods and services. The main cause has been the state of war that developed in the Middle East. That war had a major impact on our supply routes,” he said.

He said global diesel prices had risen by about 88% and petrol prices by 80% since the conflict began, and that the Government continued to subsidise diesel by Rs. 70 for every litre sold. He hoped to present several proposals in the Budget to offset the impact of fuel costs through other sectors, but did not elaborate.

“I believe we now need a new program for economic transformation,” the President said, adding that fisheries, agriculture, ports and logistics must be taken to a new level to harness the country’s full growth potential.

He said 28% of the workforce was engaged in agriculture, which contributed only 7% to GDP, underscoring low productivity and inefficiencies in the sector.

“Unless we transform the labour engaged in agriculture into productive labour, we cannot achieve a major leap in agriculture. Through various legal restrictions, extensive land laws and laws governing paddy lands, farmers have been tied down rather than liberated. If we are to take this leap, we must free farmers from the laws that bind them. That is economic transformation,” he said.

President Dissanayake said the Government was preparing plans for this, and was also working on improving the productivity of small and medium-sized industries by providing them with capital at affordable rates.

title: Tighter collection, not higher rates, to drive near-term revenue: Treasury | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:34
-     - 111

The Government on Friday said it will look to stronger tax administration and compliance, rather than new or higher tax rates, for its near-term revenue gains as it targets tax revenue of at least 17% of GDP by 2031.

This is according to a new report released by the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Ministry.

“In the near term, emphasis should be placed on increasing the productivity of existing taxes through stronger administration, rather than relying primarily on new or higher tax rates,” the Ministry said in the objectives of Sri Lanka’s Medium-Term Revenue Strategy (MTRS) 2027-2031, published on Friday.

Tax-policy measures will be phased in later, in line with implementation capacity, economic conditions and the need to maintain predictability. The tax system will be broadened and simplified so that revenue is raised from wider and more neutral bases, rather than through repeated increases in statutory rates or reliance on distortionary levies.

The objectives were published to fulfil a structural benchmark under the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Extended Fund Facility (EFF). A detailed strategy and time-bound implementation plan will follow.

The Medium-Term Fiscal Framework (MTFF) in the Fiscal Strategy Statement (FSS) 2027 projects total revenue of about 15.5% of GDP and tax revenue of about 14.2% over 2027-2031. The Ministry said the tax-to-GDP ratio had nearly doubled between 2022 and 2025, and the next phase would move from crisis-era revenue mobilisation to a durable, equitable and predictable system.

“A clear medium-term plan for revenue system reform allows taxpayers and investors to plan their activities with greater confidence, while giving administrators and policymakers a shared understanding of the sequence and timing of upcoming reforms,” the Ministry said.

Driving the near-term push, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Sri Lanka Customs (SLC) and the Excise Department will operate under a single administration model built on compliance risk management, which directs enforcement according to the risk each taxpayer poses. Wider use of the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), third-party reporting and data matching will support specialised compliance for large taxpayers, high-wealth individuals, professionals and the self-employed. Customs controls over Board of Investment (BOI) and Special Economic Zone (SEZ) activities will be tightened, and the reliability of critical systems, including the Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS), ensured.

Over the medium term, the strategy rests on four priority commitments. New corporate income tax incentives will be limited to exceptional, narrowly defined cases, subject to an assessment of additionality, meaning whether the investment would have happened without the incentive, as well as fiscal cost and economic benefits. VAT exemptions will be retained only where they effectively protect poor and vulnerable households, following an assessment of who bears the burden of the tax. Personal income tax will be reviewed to tax high-income individuals more effectively. Para-tariffs, the additional levies on imports over and above customs duty, will be phased out, with replacement measures where needed.

Exemptions and concessions across VAT, income tax, customs and investment regimes will be retained only where there is a clear economic or social justification. Existing investment incentives will be reviewed against measurable outcomes, and transfer-pricing rules, which govern pricing between related companies, tightened. The VAT base will be broadened through periodic review of exemptions, registration thresholds aligned with administrative capacity, and destination-based rules for services and intangibles, under which tax is levied where consumption takes place. Informal and digital activity will be progressively brought into the tax net.

The taxation of property, capital gains and high-value transactions will be strengthened, with any property tax framework required to be administratively feasible and to protect vulnerable households. Excises on alcohol, vehicles and other goods will be reviewed, including indexation of specific rates.

On equity, the Ministry said taxpayers in comparable circumstances would be treated consistently and those with greater capacity to pay would contribute more. Distributional analysis will be applied to VAT exemptions, retirement-income provisions and excises, with targeted social protection preferred over broad tax exemptions where feasible.

The full MTRS will include a net revenue bridge from the MTFF baseline, accounting for interactions between measures, timing and the cost of the para-tariff phase-out, rather than simply adding up expected yields.

“Where material revenue shortfalls arise, compensating measures will be identified and implemented by the Government consistent with its fiscal and debt-sustainability objectives,” the Ministry said.

Oversight will rest with the Revenue Management Committee, and performance against the strategy will be published in an annual review. The Ministry also committed to announcing major reforms well in advance, consulting affected taxpayers, and strengthening taxpayer rights, dispute resolution and refund timeliness.

“Changes in the direct-to-indirect tax composition should be treated as a structural outcome of these reforms rather than as a mechanical annual target, since the appropriate composition will also depend on economic growth, imports, inflation, compliance performance and reform sequencing,” it added.

title: Sri Lanka adds winter air links from Russia, France and Central Asia | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:33
-     - 84

Sri Lanka is set to strengthen its international air connectivity for the European winter tourism season, with several airlines introducing new services or increasing capacity on routes linking the island with Russia, France, Central Asia and Switzerland.

Flights operated by Russia’s Azur Air to Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport (MRIA) are scheduled to commence today (2), while French carrier French Bee is expected to begin services to Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in December via the Maldives.

S7 Airlines is also scheduled to launch direct flights from Siberia to Katunayake in December, operating twice weekly.

The new services come as Sri Lanka seeks to attract more visitors during the northern hemisphere’s winter season, while expanding access to emerging source markets.

Adding to the new routes, Uzbekistan’s Centrum Air last week launched direct scheduled flights between Tashkent and Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport.

Sri Lanka adds...

The twice-weekly service, operating every Wednesday and Saturday until the end of March 2027, opens another gateway from Central Asia to Sri Lanka.

Royal Spence Aviation, a partner company of Aitken Spence Travels, welcomed the launch, describing it as a step towards strengthening connectivity and tapping the potential of emerging tourism markets.

Meanwhile, Swiss airline Edelweiss is deploying additional capacity on selected high-demand routes during the peak winter season.

Colombo has received an additional weekly flight from 27 October until mid-January, increasing the airline’s frequency to up to three flights per week.

The additional capacity and new services are expected to provide more travel options for visitors and support Sri Lanka’s efforts to improve access from key and emerging international markets.

Director En Ping Ong (left) and Director/Group CEO Pravir Samarasinghe unveiling the model for Havelock City Residences

Overseas Realty (Ceylon) PLC said it has launched the development of Havelock City Residences, the fifth and final phase of Havelock City, bringing the vision of one of Colombo’s iconic integrated mixed-use projects closer to completion.

The official launch of Havelock City Residences was celebrated at a glamorous launch event held on 29 October 2026 at Hilton Colombo, attended by an exclusive gathering of invited guests.

Demonstrating strong market confidence even before its official launch, 50 % of the apartments had already been pre-sold, reflecting the continued appeal of Havelock City’s distinctive proposition- a premium residential environment combining space, greenery, connectivity, and an integrated urban lifestyle.

Set across 18 acres, Havelock City is distinguished by seven acres of beautifully landscaped gardens—the largest single enclosed green space in Sri Lanka. Designed by award winning global design firm P&T Group, Singapore, Havelock City Residences offers spacious two-, three-, and four-bedroom apartments, alongside expansive penthouses, thoughtfully planned to maximize natural light, ventilation, privacy, and views.

Residents benefit from an extensive range of recreation facilities and lifestyle amenities including landscaped walking and jogging paths, gymnasiums, squash courts, banquet halls and dedicated spaces for socializing and relaxation. The curated assisted living concept further enhances the development, promoting accessibility, independence, safety, security and peace of mind through every stage of life.

With Havelock City Mall and Mireka Office Tower integrated within the development, residents enjoy convenient access to shopping, dining, entertainment, and everyday essentials. This seamless integration of residential, commercial, and lifestyle experiences makes Havelock City a distinctive address for those seeking the convenience of city living without compromising on space and tranquility.

, Director and Group Chief Executive Officer Pravir Samarasinghe said: “The launch of Havelock City Residences marks a defining milestone in our journey to realize the vision of Havelock City as Colombo’s most sought-after integrated living destinations. 

As the fifth and final phase, Havelock City Residences brings this vision to its culmination, offering homeowners a rare combination of space, greenery, connectivity, and contemporary luxury within an established community. We are proud to bring this final chapter to market and look forward to welcoming more elite residents to the Havelock City community.”

Developed by Overseas Realty Ceylon PLC, the company behind Havelock City and the iconic World Trade Center Colombo, Havelock City Residences builds on a legacy of creating landmark real estate developments in Sri Lanka. The project is professionally managed by Realty Management Services, a wholly owned subsidiary, providing ongoing property management and hassle-free rental and resale support services.

As the final phase of Havelock City, the development presents a golden opportunity and a last chance for homeowners and investors to become part of an exclusive residential community, with the benefits of an integrated lifestyle. The project is expected to be completed in November 2030.

title: Ex-Central Banker says Govt. rejected 12% bids for $ 100 m Dollar Bond | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:29
-     - 241

The Government rejected all bids for a $ 100 million dollar-denominated Bond offered to local and diaspora investors after bidders sought yields of about 12%, a clear sign of the cost Sri Lanka will face when it returns to international capital markets, former Central Bank Deputy Governor Dr. W.A. Wijewardena said.

Speaking at CA Sri Lanka’s 28th Annual Tax Oration on Thursday, Dr. Wijewardena said the Treasury had issued the bond to test the market and had planned to increase it to $ 300 million. Instead, the entire issue was rejected after investors bid at about 12%, he said, citing available information.

“The Government did not want to show in public that the current level of market perception of Sri Lanka demands this high level of interest from the Government. It is a good thing that it did so,” he said.

Dr. Wijewardena said Sri Lanka’s sovereign rating had been upgraded to B-, with further upgrades by rating agencies expected in the first quarter of 2027, but that the country remained in the speculative grade.

“All financial experts present here know that B- is a speculative rating, which in the financial markets is known as junk rating. We are still in the junk rating category, not the investment category,” he said.

He estimated that with the 10-year US Treasury yield, the global risk-free benchmark, at around 5.6%, B- rated issuers faced a risk premium of about 5%, lifting borrowing costs to about 10.6%. Because Sri Lanka had not tapped global markets for four years, it would be treated as a new entrant on its return in 2027 or later and charged a further 1% or so.

“So altogether, the yield applicable to Sri Lanka at the current level of rating is around 11-12%, which is not affordable for Sri Lanka,” Dr. Wijewardena said.

He warned that the problem would resurface when Sri Lanka returns to the market.

“When we go to the market in 2027 or after, this problem will arise. It will be a gigantic task for Sri Lanka to raise this additional foreign exchange to meet the balance of payments gap that we are seeing,” he said.

Dr. Wijewardena also cautioned that the migration of skilled workers was eroding the country’s human capital. Universities were losing two or three academics practically every month, while Central Bank officers were also leaving despite the bank paying the highest salaries, he said.

title: Tax ‘overdose’ turning toxic, top economist warns Govt. | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:29
-     - 202

CBSL former Deputy Governor Dr. W.A. Wijewardena – Pic by Sameera Wijesingha

Former Central Bank Deputy Governor Dr. W.A. Wijewardena has called on the Government to slow its revenue drive in the 2027 Budget, warning that taxpayers are being squeezed by high income taxes, indirect taxes and inflation while receiving deteriorating public services in return.

Delivering CA Sri Lanka’s 28th Annual Tax Oration on Thursday, Dr. Wijewardena said Government revenue had risen from 12.3% of GDP in 2021 to the 15% target set under the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Extended Fund Facility (EFF), which was to be reached by 2024, and had been exceeded in 2025. He said the target was likely to be exceeded again in 2026, and in 2027 if taxes stayed at current levels.

“We outperformed the IMF, which is not a good thing, because many of you might think that when the Government raises more revenue it is good. In fact, that revenue is transferred from us. We have to sacrifice our own consumption and our own investment in order to provide that money to the Government,” he said.

Dr. Wijewardena said collections had improved through a lower personal income tax threshold, which was cut to Rs. 100,000 a month before being raised to Rs. 150,000, a marginal tax rate of 36%, and the requirement that every citizen over 18 obtain a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). VAT was raised from 8% in 2021 to 15% and then to the current 18%, while the removal of exemptions and the reduction of the VAT registration threshold to Rs. 36 million drew small firms into a more complex compliance system, he added.

He warned that indirect taxes on essential consumption made the tax system regressive, with low-income earners paying a higher share of their income in tax than high-income earners.

“It is just like a physician who gives medicine to a patient in pain. If the physician gives an overdose, the medicine will become toxic. The same thing is happening to Sri Lanka today,” he said.

Dr. Wijewardena said citizens were being hit by three types of taxes: direct taxes, which reduced disposable income; indirect taxes, which eroded the real value of purchases; and inflation, which acted as an implicit tax.

“We again experience a reduction in the real value of our financial assets when the Central Bank goes by its inflation target of 5%, or most probably 7%,” he said, referring to the upper limit of the Central Bank’s target band.

He argued that the IMF’s standard prescription relied on revenue-based fiscal consolidation, which narrows the budget gap mainly by raising revenue rather than also cutting spending, and on a primary surplus, the budget balance excluding interest payments. Critics say this protects the interest income of lenders to the Government while squeezing public servants and subsidy recipients, he noted.

The IMF had sought a primary surplus of 1.5% of GDP in 2025, but the Government achieved about 4% by curtailing capital expenditure, Dr. Wijewardena said. Of the Rs. 1.3 trillion allocated for capital expenditure in 2025, only Rs. 987 billion, or about 75%, was spent. The 2026 capital budget, also Rs. 1.3 trillion, was only 16% utilised in the first half and 28% by end-September, he said, adding that officials expected to spend the remaining 72% in the last quarter.

“If they can do so, in fact they should receive our compliments and respect for being so efficient in disposing of the capital expenditure program,” he said, warning that lower capital formation would weaken future growth and, with it, the revenue base.

Citing overcrowded wards at the National Hospital in Colombo, reliance on private tuition and delays at police stations, Dr. Wijewardena said the ‘moral contract’ between the state and taxpayers had been breached.

“This particular sacrifice that the taxpayers make is not matched by public value,” he said.

He also said the Inland Revenue Department’s Revenue Administration Management Information System (RAMIS) lacked the capacity to handle the expanded tax net, leaving taxpayers unable to file returns. He blamed this on the over-performance in tax collection and the failure to upgrade the technology available to collection agencies.

title: Current account dips back into deficit in Sept. | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:27
-     - 125

The external current account slipped back into a deficit of $ 128 million in September after recording a surplus in August, taking the cumulative deficit for the first nine months to $ 420 million.

“The deficit was lower than in September 2025, as the lower trade deficit and higher inflows of workers’ remittances outweighed the higher primary income deficit and the lower surplus in the services account,” the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) said in its External Sector Performance report for September, released on Friday.

The current account deficit stood at $ 194 million in September 2025. The January-September deficit compares with a surplus of $ 1.9 billion in the corresponding period of 2025.

The merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $ 731 million in September from $ 910 million a year earlier, as the increase in export earnings exceeded a 2.9% year-on-year (YoY) rise in import expenditure to $ 2.1 billion. The cumulative trade deficit, however, widened by about 53% to $ 7.9 billion during the first nine months from $ 5.2 billion a year earlier, as the import bill rose 21.3% to $ 18.7 billion.

“Monthly expenditure on fuel imports declined for the fifth consecutive month (month-on-month) in September 2026. However, cumulative fuel import expenditure increased by 51.5% (year-on-year) to approximately $ 4.5 billion during January-September 2026,” the CBSL said.

The terms of trade, the ratio of export prices to import prices, deteriorated YoY in September and during January-September, as import prices rose faster than export prices.

The services account surplus declined 34.3% YoY to $ 119 million in September, as outflows rose 36.7% to $ 441 million. Spending on travel abroad increased 64.9% to $ 122 million, while payments for sea and air transport services rose 49.3% to $ 140 million. Services outflows increased 24.7% to $ 3 billion during January-September, with travel abroad up 62.4% to $ 937 million and sea and air transport payments up 23.8% to $ 940 million.

“With the continued moderation in the monthly services account surplus, the cumulative services account surplus declined by 22.3% to $ 2.2 billion during January-September 2026 on a year-on-year basis,” the CBSL said.

The primary income account, which mainly captures investment income such as dividends and interest flowing in and out of the country, recorded a deficit of $ 241 million in September, against $ 152 million a year earlier. Primary income outflows rose 44.2% to $ 290 million, driven mainly by payments on direct investment, which more than doubled, rising 120.9% to $ 192 million. Interest payments on other investment fell 26.2% to $ 50 million. Over the nine months, primary income outflows declined 2.2% to $ 1.95 billion, keeping the cumulative deficit at $ 1.48 billion, below the $ 1.54 billion recorded a year earlier.

Personal transfer outflows rose 29.1% YoY to $ 10 million in September and 12.7% to $ 110 million during January-September.

On the inflow side, merchandise exports rose 21% YoY to an all-time monthly high of $ 1,377 million in September, surpassing the previous peak of $ 1,302 million in July 2025, and increased 5.3% to $ 10.8 billion during January-September. Services inflows rose 11.2% in September but slipped 0.6% to $ 5.3 billion in the nine months. Tourism earnings, estimated under a revised Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority methodology, rose 1.5% to $ 186 million in September but fell 9.2% to $ 2.2 billion cumulatively. Workers’ remittances increased 5.6% to $ 734 million in September and 18.1% to $ 6.9 billion during January-September, a figure the CBSL said may include other remittances, such as those received following Cyclone Ditwah.

title: Rupee down 6.8% YTD by  end-October; reserves at $ 6.9 b | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:25
-     - 84

The Sri Lankan rupee weakened further in October, trading at Rs. 332.61 against the US dollar by end-month, from Rs. 330.83 at end-September and Rs. 309.99 at end-2025, Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) data showed.

“By end October 2026, the Sri Lanka rupee depreciated by 6.8% against the US dollar on a year-to-date basis,” the CBSL said in its External Sector Performance report for September, released on Friday.

The rupee had depreciated 6.3% year-to-date by end-September.

“Gross official reserves by end September 2026, including the swap facility with the People’s Bank of China, stood at $ 6.9 billion,” the CBSL said.

The swap facility is a bilateral currency swap arrangement with China’s central bank, which the CBSL includes in reserves. The reserves provided import coverage of 3.3 months, a measure of how long they could finance the country’s imports.

“Foreign investment in the Government securities market recorded a net outflow of $ 39.9 million, while foreign investment in the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE), including both primary and secondary market transactions, recorded a net outflow of $ 4.7 million during September 2026,” the CBSL said.

During January-September, foreign investors recorded a net inflow of $ 168 million into Government securities, compared with $ 178 million a year earlier, while net outflows from the CSE widened to $ 170 million from $ 85 million.

title: Vehicle import bill falls 34% in Sept. | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:25
-     - 105

The country spent $ 1,871 million on motor vehicle imports during January-September, Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) data showed, about 10% of the $ 18.7 billion spent on merchandise imports in the period.

“Expenditure on motor vehicle imports, including both personal and commercial vehicles, amounted to $ 188 million in September 2026, representing a 34.4% decline compared to September 2025,” the CBSL said in its External Sector Performance report for September, released on Friday. The monthly outlay was broadly unchanged from the $ 189 million spent in August.

Despite the lower import bill, vehicle registrations rose 18% month-on-month to 54,214 units in September from 45,811 in August, led mainly by a rebound in two-wheelers and three-wheelers, according to JB Securities. Most major categories recorded gains, although volumes stayed below the levels seen earlier in 2026.

Two-wheelers drove most of the increase, climbing to 38,747 units from 33,498, of which 38,178 were brand-new. TVS topped overall two-wheeler registrations for a second straight month with 8,684 units, followed by Bajaj with 8,035 and Honda with 7,673. Bajaj remained the leader in brand-new motorcycles with 7,821 units, while Honda headed scooters with 7,532, ahead of TVS with 6,668. Financing accounted for 54.4% of two-wheeler registrations.

title: Sunshine Holdings records strong growth in 1HFY27 with revenue up 24.4% and PAT rising 44.3% | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 05:45
-     - 139

CEO Shyam Sathasivam

Diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate Sunshine Holdings PLC (CSE: SUN) reported strong top-line and bottom-line growth during the six months ended 30 September 2026 (1HFY27), recording a consolidated revenue of Rs. 40.2 billion, an increase of 24.4% year-on-year (YoY). The Group’s profit after tax (PAT) increased by 44.3% YoY to Rs. 3.7 billion, supported by the resilience of the Group’s diversified portfolio across Healthcare, Consumer and Agribusiness

Healthcare remained the largest contributor to Group revenue, accounting for 49% of the total, followed by Consumer at 37% and Agribusiness at 14%. The Group’s gross profit increased by 11.7% YoY to Rs. 11.5 billion, while its gross profit margin stood at 28.7%, compared to 31.9% in the corresponding period last year, primarily reflecting regulated pharmaceutical price reductions and the impact of a weaker rupee on the Healthcare sector.

Group earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) increased by 10.5% YoY to Rs. 6.1 billion, while the EBIT margin stood at 15.1%, compared to 17% in 1HFY26. Higher net finance income and a lower effective tax rate supported the Group’s profitability, with the PAT margin improving to 9.2% from 8% in the previous year. The Group also recorded stronger second-quarter momentum, with revenue increasing by 32% YoY to Rs. 21.6 billion and PAT growing by 82.4% YoY to Rs. 2.3 billion.

Commenting on the performance, Sunshine Holdings PLC Group CEO Shyam Sathasivam said, “Our first-half performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our ability to deliver growth across all three sectors. While regulatory pricing pressures and currency movements continue to affect margins, we have maintained our focus on operational efficiency and strategic expansion. Our investments in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, digital healthcare and export-oriented businesses are important steps towards strengthening our long-term competitiveness. We remain committed to building resilient businesses and creating sustainable value for our stakeholders.”

The Group’s Healthcare sector recorded revenue of Rs. 19.6 billion during 1HFY27, representing a 13.3% YoY increase. Growth accelerated during the second quarter, with revenue rising by 20.5% YoY. The sector’s EBIT margin however, declined to 11.2% from 13.1% in 1HFY26, mainly due to regulated price reductions and the impact of a weaker rupee on imported products. The Pharmaceutical agency segment recorded a 24% YoY revenue contraction, mainly due to a change in operating model compared to last year, lower shipments from certain principals and regulatory-related stock shortages. Medical Devices and Healthguard Distribution recorded revenue growth of 19.9% and 4.1% YoY, respectively, while Healthguard Pharmacy remained broadly stable. Lina Manufacturing, the Group’s pharmaceutical manufacturing arm, delivered a strong performance with revenue increasing by 35.1% YoY, supported by deliveries against government orders.

During the period, Sunshine Holdings also advanced its commitment to strengthening local pharmaceutical manufacturing by finalising the joint venture agreement with India’s Zydus Lifesciences Limited. The joint venture signed an agreement with the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI) to develop a GMP-compliant oral solid dosage manufacturing facility at the Horana Export Processing Zone.

Further strengthening its healthcare portfolio, Sunshine Healthcare Lanka Limited acquired a 21.92% stake in Digital Health Ltd, operator of the Doc990 platform, in October 2026, following the reporting period. This investment expands the Group’s presence in digital healthcare services, complementing its existing pharmaceutical agency, distribution, manufacturing and retail operations.

The Group’s Consumer sector delivered strong revenue growth of 53.5% YoY to Rs. 15 billion in 1HFY27, primarily driven by the consolidation of JAPC and the recovery of its tea export business. Excluding JAPC, sector revenue increased by 13% YoY, supported by growth in branded tea and tea exports. The sector’s EBIT margin improved to 8.0% from 7.8% in the corresponding period last year.

The Branded Tea business recorded revenue growth of 5.6% YoY, led by Watawala Thei, while Zesta continued to operate in a highly competitive premium tea market. The Confectionery business registered a 2.2% YoY revenue increase, supported by growth in gums and wafers, which offset declines in toffee and candy categories.

The Tea Export business recorded a strong recovery, with revenue increasing by 25.4% YoY during 1HFY27. Second-quarter revenue grew by 60.9% YoY, driven by additional business from key customers and a higher contribution from value-added tea products.

Meanwhile, JAPC’s spice export revenue grew by 28.6%, supported by demand across its key product categories. The consolidation of JAPC further strengthened the Consumer sector’s export portfolio, expanding the Group’s presence in the spice export business.

The Group’s Agribusiness sector, represented by Watawala Plantations PLC (CSE: WATA), recorded revenue of Rs. 5.6 billion during 1HFY27, reflecting a 7.2% YoY increase, primarily driven by the oil palm business.

Oil palm revenue grew by 9.1% YoY to Rs. 5 billion, supported by increased own-crop production. However, growth moderated during the second quarter due to lower bought-crop availability and reduced oil extraction rates.

The Dairy business recorded revenue of Rs. 561.1 million, a decline of 2.9% YoY, as higher selling prices partly offset lower milk sales volumes. While the business continued to face higher effluent management costs, operating performance improved during the second quarter. The Agribusiness sector’s EBIT margin stood at 47.8%, compared to 49.1% in 1HFY26, reflecting higher operating costs in the oil palm business.

During the period, Sunshine Holdings also increased its stake in Watawala Plantations PLC to 77.02% through Sunshine Wilmar Ltd. Separately, Watawala Plantations acquired the remaining non-controlling interest in Lonach Dairy Limited, making it a wholly owned subsidiary.

title: COYLE’s “I AM” Leadership Forum 2026 concludes with a focus on stories that shape leaders | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 05:25
-     - 64

Chief Guest Indian High Commissioner of India to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha (centre) along with COYLE Chairman Suren Chandraratna (fourth from right) , COYLE Committee Chairman Raveen Wickramasinghe (left), Sensa Solutions Managing Director Subash Thalangama (third from right), Tudawe Brothers CEO Romali Tudawe (second fro right), and hSenid Group of Companies Founder/Chairman Dinesh Saparamadu (second from left)

The Chamber of Lankan Entrepreneurs (COYLE) concluded its “I AM” Leadership Forum 2026 at Cinnamon Grand Colombo last week, bringing together entrepreneurs and business leaders for an evening of personal stories, shared experience and dialogue on leadership. The event was made possible by principle sponsor, Nations Trust Bank, along with print media sponsors, DailyFT and The Sunday Times.

Held under the theme “My Story. My Journey”, the forum reflected COYLE’s broader vision for 2026 of “Bridging Generations. Building Futures”, creating space for established and emerging entrepreneurs to learn from one another.

Indian High Commissioner Santosh Jha, graced the occasion as Chief Guest and keynote speaker. His participation brought an international dimension to the forum and underscored the value of dialogue between the diplomatic and business communities.

In his welcome address, COYLE Chairman Suren Chandraratna challenged participants to consider the question at the heart of the forum: “Who am I?” Drawing on his own experience as a panellist the previous year, he described the ‘I AM’ platform as an opportunity to reflect on what entrepreneurs have achieved, overcome and become. “When a person discovers their ‘I AM’, they stop being defined by where they come from, what others said they could be, or limitations placed upon them. They begin to see not just who they are today, but who they can become tomorrow,” he said.

Chandraratna also placed entrepreneurial development at the centre of Sri Lanka’s economic future. “We believe that it is the Sri Lankan entrepreneurs who can unlock the golden opportunities that our economy has,” he said, emphasising COYLE’s role in empowering entrepreneurs to discover their potential and share experiences that can inspire others.

The forum featured panelists Sensa Solutions Managing Director Subash Thalangama, Tudawe Brothers CEO Romali Tudawe, and hSenid Group of Companies Founder/Chairman Dinesh Saparamadu, in a discussion moderated by Dr.Tharindu Ameresekera. Bringing perspectives from different businesses and industries, the speakers placed their personal journeys at the centre of the conversation.

Their experiences opened up a discussion about the demands of entrepreneurship: making difficult decisions, navigating uncertainty, responding to setbacks and finding the resolve to move forward. For participants, the value lay in connecting these experiences with the challenges and choices in their own businesses.

The theme “My Story. My Journey” gave the evening a clear focus. Every business is shaped by people, and every leader carries lessons that others can learn from. Creating opportunities to share those lessons is central to building stronger connections between generations of entrepreneurs.

COYLE Committee Chairman Raveen Wickramasinghe delivering the vote of thanks said, “The true value of this forum will be measured by what we do next, how we apply what we have learnt, support another entrepreneur and turn a new connection into an opportunity. Each story shared tonight reminds us that experience becomes more powerful when it helps someone else move forward. Let us carry that spirit into our businesses and help more Sri Lankan entrepreneurs succeed.”

The ‘I AM’ Leadership Forum 2026 reinforced COYLE’s commitment to developing a business community in which experience is shared and emerging leaders have access to those who have navigated the journey before them. Its purpose extended beyond a single evening: to encourage entrepreneurs to carry those lessons into the decisions they make, the businesses they build and the people they lead.

title: Tisara De Silva inducted as President of OPA for 2026/2027 | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 05:23
-     - 66

Tisara De Silva

Tisara De Silva was inducted as President of the Organisation of Professional Associations of Sri Lanka (OPA) for the term 2026 to 2027 at 51st organisation’s Annual General Meeting held on 30 October 2026. 

His elevation to the Presidency marks a significant milestone for the Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka (PSSL), as he becomes the first professional from (PSSL)

 to assume the presidency of OPA which is founded in 1975, OPA serves as the apex body representing 52 Member Associations across 32 professions. Its role in bringing together diverse professional disciplines provides an important platform for collective engagement, policy dialogue and constructive contributions to national development.

His election as President-Elect of OPA in the preceding year, secured with a high majority of votes, reflected the confidence placed in his leadership and the esteem in which he is held within the professional community. 

De Silva brings to the Presidency extensive institutional experience, professional insight and a longstanding commitment to organisational development. He served as General Secretary of OPA for two consecutive years, 2023-2024 and 2024-2025, and as Chairman of the Premises Maintenance Committee. In 2022- 2023 he served as Vice-President of OPA and Chairman of the Seminars, Workshops and Programs Committee. Further, his involvement in the Executive Council over many years and his 23-years experiences and association with the OPA General Forum reflect a sustained commitment to the organisation’s governance, activities and wider professional mission.

A past pupil of Royal College, Colombo 7, De Silva is a distinguished member of the Pharmaceutical profession and a Past President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka (PSSL). Over more than 26 years of service on the PSSL Council, he has held numerous leadership positions, including President for two consecutive terms (2020–2021 and 2021–2022), Immediate Past President, President-Elect, Senior Vice-President, Vice-President, Assistant Secretary and Council Member. He has also served for several years as a member of the Society’s Board of Trustees. De Silva is a Pharmacist registered with the Sri Lanka Medical Council.

His professional career spans more than 32 years in the Pharmaceutical Industry, including 27 years in senior management at GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals, a leading Multinational Pharmaceutical Company. This experience has provided him with extensive exposure to pharmaceutical operations, organisational management and leadership within an international corporate environment.

His academic and professional development includes a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from Malaysia, a Diploma in Modern Management from the United Kingdom, and a Diploma in Computer Programming. This combination of professional experience, management expertise and educational background has shaped his contributions to institutional leadership and the advancement of the pharmaceutical sector. 

Beyond his national responsibilities, De Silva has maintained an active presence in Regional and International Pharmaceutical Organisations. He currently serves as Secretary of Pharmaceutical Sciences of the South East Asian Regional Pharmaceutical Forum (SEARPharm Forum) and as a member of its Executive Council until 2027.From 2020 to 2022, he served as a Bureau Member of the Federation of Asian Pharmaceutical Associations (FAPA) and as a Council Member of the International Pharmaceutical Federation (FIP). He is also a member of the Commonwealth Pharmaceutical Association (CPA), United Kingdom. These engagements reflect his continuing contribution to professional collaboration, knowledge exchange and the representation of pharmaceutical interests beyond national boundaries. 

De Silva’s assumption of the OPA Presidency is a considerable pride for the Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka. His achievement underscores the contribution of the pharmaceutical profession and industry to the broader professional landscape and affirms the value of sustained participation in collective professional leadership.

As he undertakes this responsibility as president of OPA for 2026 to 2027, his extensive experience in professional governance, industry leadership and international engagement provides a strong foundation for serving the OPA and its diverse membership.

title: Govt. to finalise disaster risk financing strategy by mid-2027 | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 06:06
-     - 46

Sri Lanka’s National Disaster Risk Financing Strategy is expected to be finalised by mid-2027, the Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development said, following a stakeholder workshop on its preparation.

The PDMO is leading the development of the strategy with technical assistance from the Asian Development Bank (ADB). It aims to strengthen national financial resilience, protect development gains and enhance the Government’s capacity to manage the fiscal impact of natural disasters.

The workshop, held on 21 October, brought together disaster risk management stakeholders, relevant Government institutions, development partners and insurance industry representatives. It focused on the need for a comprehensive strategy to strengthen financial preparedness for natural disasters, health emergencies, energy supply and food price shocks, and other situations within its scope.

Discussions highlighted the need to identify and assess disaster-related fiscal risks, select appropriate financing instruments and adopt a risk-layering approach, under which different financing tools are matched to disasters of different frequency and severity, to ensure timely and sustainable funding for response and recovery while safeguarding fiscal stability.

The PDMO said the active engagement of key stakeholders would be important in developing a practical and sustainable strategy aligned with Sri Lanka’s requirements.

title: Tamil leaders take anti-terror law fears to UK envoy | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 05:55
-     - 36

Tamil political leaders last week met British High Commissioner Andrew Patrick to convey concerns that the Government’s proposed anti-terrorism and organised crime laws could be used against minority communities, with the envoy expressing deep concern over the anti-terrorism legislation, according to the Tamil Eelam Liberation Organization (TELO).

TELO Leader and Democratic Tamil National Alliance (DTNA) MP Selvam Adaikkalanathan and TELO Vice President and Spokesperson and DTNA Deputy National Organiser Guruswamy Surendran discussed with the High Commissioner the risks posed to the country, and to minority communities in particular, by the Protection of the State from Terrorism Act (PSTA) and the Organised Crime Bill presented to Parliament by the Government.

The TELO leaders said the proposed laws could be used to suppress, or facilitate the arbitrary and targeted arrest of, those campaigning on long-standing issues, including the demand for a permanent political solution for Tamils in the Northern and Eastern Provinces, land grabbing, enforced disappearances, war crimes, human rights violations, the need for a justice mechanism and the repeated postponement of Provincial Council elections.

They noted that while UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC) reports had called for the repeal of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), the Government was instead attempting to introduce alternative legislation that posed a significant threat to Tamils and the country as a whole. They also said the continued delay in holding Provincial Council elections had left their regions without a provincial administrative structure, which in turn facilitated land grabbing by State institutions.

On the wider political climate, the TELO leaders said excessive taxation and uncontrollable price increases were severely affecting livelihoods, not only of those below the poverty line but of the broader population. They also told the High Commissioner that six Tamil-speaking political parties represented in Parliament were working together on issues of common concern.

According to TELO, the High Commissioner responded that the need to hold Provincial Council elections had been highlighted in UNHRC reports. On the anti-terrorism legislation, he said the UK had closely monitored such proposals in the past, which had appeared in various guises, and remained deeply concerned about the current version, TELO said.

title: Supreme Court orders Dompe cop to pay Rs. 100,000 for assaulting woman | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 2 November 2026 05:44
-     - 30

The Supreme Court has ordered a Police Constable attached to the Dompe Police Station to pay Rs. 100,000 in compensation from his personal funds within six months, after holding that he violated the fundamental rights of a woman by physically assaulting her.

A three-judge bench comprising Justices Janak De Silva, Menaka Wijesundera and Sampath Wijeratne made the determination while allowing a fundamental rights petition filed by Jayasinghage Nirmala Kanthi.

The Court declared that the first respondent, Police Constable Lakmal (84253), had infringed the petitioner’s fundamental right guaranteed under Article 11 of the Constitution, which prohibits torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

The petitioner alleged that she was physically and verbally assaulted by the constable on 7 October, 2019, when she visited the Dompe Police Station to deliver a lunch packet to her husband. He had been arrested by Special Task Force officers over an allegation of brewing illicit liquor.

In support of her case, she produced medical documents, including a medico-legal examination receipt and a diagnosis ticket, along with photographs of her injuries. The Court observed that the injuries in the photographs appeared to correspond with those recorded in the medical documents.

Her account was further corroborated by an affidavit from the three-wheeler driver who took her to the police station and later drove her to hospital for treatment.

Senior Counsel Himalee Kularatne appeared for the petitioner. Counsel Udaya Bandara, instructed by Kalana De Silva, appeared for the first respondent, while State Counsel Induni Punchihewa appeared for the Attorney General.

title: Bay of Bengal depression to intensify into severe cyclonic storm today | Daily FT

A depression over the Southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal today, the Department of Meteorology warned.

The system, moving west-northwestwards, was forecast to develop into a deep depression over the Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal around 11.30 a.m. yesterday, and to intensify into a cyclonic storm around 11.30 p.m.

The Department warned that wind speeds in the affected sea areas could occasionally reach 70-80 kmph, accompanied by heavy showers or thundershowers, with sea conditions expected to become very rough.

Meanwhile, showers or thundershowers were forecast after 1.00 p.m. yesterday in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Uva and Southern Provinces, as well as in the Ampara and Batticaloa districts, with dry weather expected in other parts of the island.
